editorial.headline: Other Wood Panels: Open Nationally, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 16219 covers engineered wood-panel manufacturing, open nationally to foreign ownership but blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the recorded moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 16219 is the manufacturing category for other wood panels: engineered sheets made from wood fibre, particles, strands, chips, or honeycomb structures. The record names fibreboard explicitly, including low density fibreboard, medium density fibreboard, and high density fibreboard, alongside particle board, oriented strand board, chip board, and honeycomb board. In plain English, this is not furniture making or timber trading; it is the industrial production of panel materials that other builders, fabricators, or manufacturers may later use.

The activity is open across the scales listed in the record: Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the code is not framed as a narrow large-factory category only; the record presents it as available to small, medium, and large operators. For founders, the practical reading is that the code can describe a range of wood-panel production setups, from smaller manufacturing operations to larger industrial facilities, as long as the registered activity is genuinely the making of these panel products.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is straightforward. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership figure in the record is 100%, with the cited national basis being Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national layer alone, that means the code is recorded as foreign-open, with no lower ownership ceiling shown in the slim record. There is no basis here to invent a special licence, capital threshold, tax condition, or extra timing rule; the record gives the national opening, the ownership ceiling, the source, and the permitted scales.

Bali is the decisive complication. The record marks this activity as blocked for PMA registration in Bali, with the status Blocked (risk class). The stated reason is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule is also stated directly: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest reading is this: KBLI 16219 may be nationally foreign-open, but a foreigner cannot register it as a PMA activity in Bali today under the record provided.
